audit: Cohort has 1731 cases; 81 have diagnosis 'missing' and 25 'Unknown' (excluded), and 81 lack site. Mutation burden is extremely skewed: 18 hypermutators with >200 mutations (max 15731 in one case) were excluded from the analysis; burden differs by diagnosis (pilocytic astrocytoma median 2 vs medulloblastoma 13), and 26 of 168 pilocytic astrocytomas and 124 cases overall have zero mutations, which suggests heterogeneous source studies or calling pipelines. Diagnosis labels are coarse and heterogeneous (e.g. 'Glioma, malignant' mixes many entities, 'Neoplasm, malignant' is a catch-all), and no ancestry, treatment, sample-purity or source-study fields exist, so batch confounding cannot be excluded. Enrichment is against the rest of the cohort, which is dominated by other brain tumours, so the comparator is not neutral. Some hits look technical: H3C2 (a multi-copy histone gene, 6 cases, 0 elsewhere) and ZMYM3 are suspect for mapping artefacts, so they were not claimed. Small-denominator diagnoses (n<15) give unstable rates. Probabilities are subjective judgements from q-value, effect size, sample size and biology, not calibrated estimates.
methods: Excluded cases with 'missing', 'Unknown' or empty diagnosis, and hypermutators (>200 non-synonymous mutations; 18 cases). For each diagnosis with at least 5 usable cases, and each gene mutated in at least 3 usable cases with at least 2 mutated cases in that diagnosis, I ran a one-sided Fisher exact test (diagnosis vs rest of usable cohort, counting cases with at least one mutation in the gene), giving 848 tests, Benjamini-Hochberg corrected. expected_frequency is Laplace-smoothed ((a+1)/(n+2)) within the diagnosis. Claims were chosen from the top of the BH-corrected list on biological plausibility and avoidance of likely artefacts; 'established' reflects my recall of the literature, not a database search. Standard library Python only; no external data used.
